subject: Banking
title: Why Banks Are So Profitable
description: A quick, practical guide to Why Banks Are So Profitable.

hook.text: JPMorgan earned $49 billion in profit in 2023. That's more than most countries' GDP. Banking is insanely profitable.

buildup.text: Banks combine interest income, fee income, trading revenue, and wealth management.

discovery.text: Leverage amplifies returns. Banks hold $10 in assets for every $1 in capital.

twist.text: Bank profits are partly subsidized by taxpayers. Deposit insurance, central bank lending.

climax.text: Banking is profitable because it's leveraged, diversified, and backstopped by government.

punchline.text: $49 billion in one year. Leveraged, diversified, and government-backed.

quiz.question: How much profit did JPMorgan earn in 2023?

details.summary: Banks are among the most consistently profitable industries because they borrow at low cost from depositors, lend at higher rates, operate with significant leverage, and benefit from government safety nets that reduce their risk at taxpayer expense.
details.whyItMatters: Bank profitability is subsidized by government insurance and central bank backstops. Understanding this reveals that bank profits are partly a transfer from taxpayers who bear the tail risk of bank failures.
takeaways: US banks earned over $260 billion in net income in 2023
Deposit insurance lets banks borrow cheaply because depositors feel safe
Government backstops socialize losses while privatizing profits

faq.question: How does government support make banks more profitable?
faq.answer: Deposit insurance lets banks borrow at nearly risk-free rates since depositors know they will be repaid. Access to Fed lending provides a safety net that reduces funding costs. These implicit guarantees would cost billions if banks had to purchase them privately.

faq.question: Are banks more profitable than other industries?
faq.answer: Banks consistently rank among the most profitable sectors by return on equity. The combination of leverage, cheap deposit funding, fee income, and government safety nets creates a business model that regularly delivers 10-15% returns on equity.
